title: You can fake a smile.
paragraphs:
You can fake a smile.
You can fake a prayer.
But you can’t fake your spiritual condition before God.
Let’s get honest.

Not with people.
With Him.

Here are 6 questions that don’t flatter—
they expose.
1. When no one is watching… who are you becoming?

Not what you post.
Not what you say in church.
But in the dark—your thoughts, your habits, your cravings.
“Man looks at the outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart.” (1 Samuel 16:7)
Your secret life is your real life.
2. Do you run to God… or hide from Him when you sin?

Conviction draws you closer.
Shame pushes you away.

Adam hid.
David ran back weeping.

Same sin nature.
Different response.

One leads to death.
The other to mercy.
3. Is your Bible opened… or just your notifications?
Be honest.

How many hours scrolling?
How many minutes in the Word?
Jesus said, “Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word…” (Matthew 4:4)

You are feeding something every day.
The question is—what?
4. Do you love holiness… or just hate consequences?

Some people don’t hate sin.
They hate getting caught.

That’s not repentance.
That’s damage control.

True repentance says:
“Lord, change my heart—even if no one ever finds out.”
5. Is your faith producing fruit… or just feelings?

Tears in worship are not proof.
Goosebumps are not evidence.
Jesus said, “You will know them by their fruits.” (Matthew 7:16)

Are you becoming more patient?
More pure?
More like Christ?
Or just more emotional?
6. If Jesus returned tonight… would you be ready—or exposed?

Not your pastor.
Not your family.
You.
Face to face with a holy God.

No filters.
No excuses.
Just truth.
But here’s what we miss…
This is not a checklist to condemn you.
It’s a mirror to lead you home.

Because the Gospel is not:
“Fix yourself, then come.”

The Gospel is:
“Come broken—and I will make you new.”

Jesus didn’t die for your polished version.
He died for the real you—the one behind the mask.
“He who conceals his sins does not prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them finds mercy.” (Proverbs 28:13)
Pause.
Ask yourself—honestly.

And if something in you just got exposed…
good.
That’s not rejection.
That’s invitation.

Come back to Jesus.
Not tomorrow.
Now.

Repent.
Receive grace.
Start again.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
